title: A single algebraic diagnostic detects structurally identical phase transitions from quarks to the cosmic horizon
object_of_study: heterogeneity/coherence signatures across physical phase boundaries
main_question: Does the same algebraic heterogeneity diagnostic exhibit comparable boundary behavior across physical systems separated by extreme scale?

claim_layers.claim: IC/F exhibits structurally identical phase-transition signatures across systems from quark confinement to dark-energy cosmology; Δ spikes at every phase boundary tested (Crossref abstract).
11,342 automated proofs across 406 physical objects confirm F+ω≡1, IC≤F, IC=exp(κ) to machine precision with zero violations.
The library places this as diagnostic material with a domain-translation secondary role; it records no claim of mechanistic identity.

source_boundary: The governing source is SRC-000017 ("A single algebraic diagnostic detects structurally identical phase transitions from quarks to the cosmic horizon"). The source establishes only what its own public record and text state; everything classified here under the current Structura Reditus architecture (Tier-2 class, structural focus, evidence mode, maturity) is library interpretation and is not attributed to the source.
authority_boundary: This is a Tier-2 Research Library object. Library admission does not grant Tier-0 protocol authority or Tier-1 kernel authority.
scope: The IC/F ratio and heterogeneity gap Δ = F − IC computed from one algebraic kernel over normalised physical measurements across systems spanning 61 orders of magnitude and 20 scientific domains, with computational verification of the three identities.
exclusions: Does not claim that the underlying domain mechanisms are identical; only that the diagnostic's boundary signatures are structurally comparable.
Does not claim the AM-GM bound as a contribution.
Publication state is preprint; publication status carries no admission authority.
preserved_meaning: The source's own scoping: the contribution is the systematic application of a scale-independent diagnostic, not the bound itself; the diagnostic is stated to be independent of the underlying dynamics.
